0.0.n: 月 after a number names the month here.

0.1.n: Makes October an approximate starting point.

0.2.n: Marks the start of the marathon season.

0.3.n: 月 after 3 names the third month.

0.4.n: Makes March an approximate ending point.

0.5.n: Marks the endpoint of the period introduced with から.

0.6.n: Casually marks the whole October-to-March period as the topic.

0.7.n: This borrowed word describes the type of season through の.

0.8.n: Links マラソン to シーズン, specifying what the season is for.

0.9.n: Refers to the time of year when marathon events take place.

0.10.n: だ changes to な before ので when following a noun.

0.11.n: Introduces the reason for the race participation described next.

1.0.n: Points back to the October-to-March period.

1.1.n: Literally means inside; その中 refers to within the previously mentioned season.

1.2.n: Marks that period as the setting for the race participation.

1.3.n: 回 counts occurrences, here the number of times the speaker enters races.

1.4.n: Presents one and two as alternative numbers of races.

1.5.n: 回 counts occurrences rather than individual objects.

1.6.n: Emphasizes one or two races as a baseline, with a possible contrast to doing fewer.

1.7.n: Short for フルマラソン, distinguishing the full distance from shorter races.

1.8.n: Links フル to 大会 to identify the race distance.

1.9.n: Refers to an organized marathon competition here.

1.10.n: Marks the event the speaker participates in with 出る.

1.11.n: Plain form of 出る; 大会に出る means taking part in a competition.

1.12.n: Casual form of という, linking the preceding description to 感じ.

1.13.n: Softens the description into an approximate account of the speaker's usual routine.

1.14.n: Adds politeness after the noun 感じ.

1.15.n: Softens the ending and invites the listener's understanding.

0.lit: From around October until around March, as for that, because it is marathon season,
0.tip: って casually marks the time period as the topic, while なので gives the reason for what follows.

1.lit: Within that, once or twice at least, participating in full-marathon events—that is the general pattern, you know.
1.tip: っていう感じです softens the statement to something like that's roughly my usual pattern.
